From the actual 20 vertices, 60 edges, 30 squares, independent reconstruction gives a connected oriented closed genus-six cubical surface and Lefschetz counts L(g)=6,2,0 for double transpositions, 3-cycles and 5-cycles. The signed graph H1 traces are -2,0,1; with H2 orientation invariant under A5, L=2-2 tr(H1(K5)). Finite orientation-preserving periodic surface maps have isolated fixed points of local index +1 and cyclic point stabilizers. Counting 15 order-two and 20 order-three group elements yields three stabilizer-two branch orbits and one stabilizer-three orbit; Riemann-Hurwitz yields quotient genus zero. A signed fundamental cycle proves S5 orientation sign and particle exchange reversal. This is a correct finite-case calculation, NOT a general assertion inferred from testing.

originality.rationale: FAIL due to decisive prior stronger coverage, not a failed search. Farb–Looijenga (2019 arXiv:1912.12280, published 2020), Section 2.1, explicitly quotes Dolgachev–Farb–Looijenga Proposition 3.2: ANY genus-six compact Riemann surface with faithful A5 action has orbifold signature (0;3,2,2,2). The natural A5 action on the audited genus-six PL surface is faithful and orientation preserving; finite oriented surface actions can be given invariant conformal structures and thus fall within this theorem. Consequently the exact main quotient result and branch orbit counts are implied, not novel. Earlier work even discusses the K5 configuration in this genus-six A5 setting. The elementary S5 sign/particle-swap observations are additional but cannot make the already-covered original main claim pass.
residual_risks: The quotient statement is decisively covered, regardless of any separate novelty in an orientation-character observation.
The cited smoothing/invariant-conformal-structure transfer is standard finite surface-action theory; no claim that the combinatorial K5 surface is the same complex algebraic member is needed.
The independent computation was a mathematical consistency check, not external expert validation.
